Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 1, Verse 1

“Dhritarashtra said: What did the sons of Pandu and my own sons do, O Sanjaya, when they assembled, eager to fight, on the sacred field of Kurukshetra?”

The Gita opens with a blind king's anxious question. Dhritarashtra's own words betray him — he separates "my sons" from "Pandu's sons," revealing the attachment and partiality that will drive the entire tragedy. The battlefield is called dharma-kshetra, the field of righteousness, hinting that this is more than a war — it is a test of conscience.
